chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudaylah from Husayn from Ibn Muskān and Muḥammad ibn Sinān from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said:

"When you begin your prayer with 'Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad' and you intend to read with it (instead of Al-Fātiḥah), then proceed with it and do not return (to Al-Fātiḥah) unless it is Friday, for you return to Al-Fātiḥah and the Muḥāfiqūn from it."

key_terms.اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ: The hypocrites (or those who are careful/attentive in this context)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اَللّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas instead of Surah Al-Fatiha in prayer, especially on Friday?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* highlights the distinct Friday prayer etiquette, where reciting Al-Fātiḥah is preferred over Al-Ikhlas to align with the communal practice and the specific virtues of the day. The mention of 'Al-Munāfiqūn' (the hypocrites) in the context of Friday prayers likely alludes to the Friday prayer of the hypocrites in Medina, emphasizing the spiritual significance of adhering to the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams on this holy day. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unique status of Friday as a day of gathering and spiritual renewal.
